suggestions.how: Say 'The aim is X'. If the action does not serve X, change it.
suggestions.check: Your starts hit the target.

suggestions.title: Plan the first three steps
suggestions.do: Write the first three steps before acting.
suggestions.how: Even in a rush, jot the three steps. Act on step one.
suggestions.check: Your early actions fit into the whole plan.

suggestions.title: Check with one person
suggestions.do: Share your plan with one other person before you start.
suggestions.how: Say it in one sentence. Ask 'Does that make sense?'.
suggestions.check: You catch weak plans early.

suggestions.title: Review impulsive starts
suggestions.do: Log each impulsive start and its result.
suggestions.how: Write one line: what I did, what happened, what I would do next. Read weekly.
suggestions.check: You see the pattern and shift to considered starts.

suggestions.title: Anticipate the next need
suggestions.do: Spot what the group will need in two minutes and act now.
suggestions.how: Ask 'What will we need next?' and prepare it.
suggestions.check: You are always a step ahead.

suggestions.title: Start something new in your community
suggestions.do: Begin a small original project that others can join.
suggestions.how: A reading drive, a fitness group, a clean-up. Run it for a month.
suggestions.check: Others join and it continues.

olq.name: Self Confidence
olq.meaning: How steadily you believe in your own ability to deal with a situation, without needing reassurance and without overstating yourself.
olq.trainNote: SC is trainable, and the advice is opposite for the under-confident Aspirant and the over-confident one. SC also influences POE, INI, COUR and SA.

tick.6: Adequate. You carry yourself with reasonable confidence. The step up is staying steady under pressure and with seniors.
tick.7: Restricted. Confidence shows in familiar settings and wavers in new ones, or is a little overstated.
tick.8: Limitation. Confidence is low and shows as hesitation, or is inflated and shows as showing off.
tick.9: Serious limitation. Confidence is either very low or very distorted, so the basics of steady self belief need rebuilding.

olq.strength: Strength. You carry yourself with steady confidence. Keep testing it in harder rooms.

patterns.label: Under-confident, needs reassurance

seen.6: Confident and a little unsure in new settings.
seen.7: Wavers in new settings and with seniors. Looks for reassurance.
seen.8: Diffident. Doubts own ability and hesitates to speak or act.
seen.9: Very low belief in own ability. Avoids challenge.

patterns.root: Fear of failure or of judgement. Past setbacks have stuck.

patterns.label: Confident at ease, shaky under pressure

seen.6: Steady, with a dip under high pressure.
seen.7: Confident in familiar settings and rattled when pressed.
seen.8: Loses confidence under pressure or challenge. Voice and ideas shrink.
seen.9: Collapses under pressure.

patterns.root: Confidence is tied to comfort. It has not been tested enough under stress.

patterns.label: Overconfident, shows off

seen.6: Confident, with a slight tendency to oversell.
seen.7: Confident and a little too sure of own view.
seen.8: Overconfident. Boasts, overstates and does not listen.
seen.9: Arrogant and unaware of weaknesses.

patterns.root: Wants to be seen as capable. Little honest feedback so far.

patterns.label: Depends on others' approval

seen.6: Confident, and seeks some approval.
seen.7: Confident when praised, less when not.
seen.8: Looks to others to validate every move. Changes view with each response.
seen.9: No steady view without constant approval.

patterns.root: Self worth is linked to praise.

patterns.label: Confident look, thin ability underneath

seen.6: Confident, and the content sometimes trails the style.
seen.7: Looks confident while content is limited.
seen.8: Style outruns substance. Falls apart when probed.
seen.9: Bluffs. Confidence disappears at the first real test.

patterns.root: Presentation skills ahead of preparation and knowledge.

patterns.label: Consolidate and stretch

seen.5: Strength. Keep testing it in harder rooms.
seen.6: Confident and steady. Gains come from staying that way under pressure and with seniors.

patterns.root: Strong base. The gap to a stronger tick is steadiness under tests.

suggestions.title: Win log
suggestions.do: Write three things you did well every night.
suggestions.how: Specific wins only: 'I spoke first in the session', 'I fixed the bike'. Read the list on Sunday.
suggestions.check: You see evidence of ability and your self-talk improves.

suggestions.title: Do one thing that scares you a little
suggestions.do: Take one small risk every day.
suggestions.how: Speak up in class, ask a question, call someone. Raise the risk slowly.
suggestions.check: The fear shrinks with every repeat.

suggestions.title: Prepare so you know your material
suggestions.do: Know your points before every group or interview practice.
suggestions.how: Prepare two facts and one view on likely topics. Real preparation builds quiet confidence.
suggestions.check: You enter the room with something to say.

suggestions.title: Stand tall and speak in a clear voice
suggestions.do: Fix posture, eye contact and voice before you speak.
suggestions.how: Stand straight, shoulders back, look at the person. Practise a clear first sentence.
suggestions.check: You look and feel steady.

suggestions.title: Rehearse under pressure
suggestions.do: Practise in mock sessions where someone pushes you.
suggestions.how: Ask a mentor or friend to interrupt, challenge and press. Keep your answer steady.
suggestions.check: You stay steady when pushed.

suggestions.title: Breathe before you answer
suggestions.do: Take one slow breath before replying to a hard question.
suggestions.how: Breathe in for four and out for six. Answer after the breath.
suggestions.check: Your voice and ideas stay steady.

suggestions.title: Hold your view for one challenge
suggestions.do: When challenged, restate your view with a reason before you change it.
suggestions.how: Say 'My reason is...' and wait. Change only if the argument is better.
suggestions.check: You neither collapse nor dig in.

suggestions.title: Rehearse failure
suggestions.do: Practise a recovery after a bad answer.
suggestions.how: Make a mistake deliberately in practice and carry on calmly. Say 'Let me rephrase'.
suggestions.check: A slip does not throw you.

suggestions.title: Ask for honest feedback
suggestions.do: Ask two people to tell you where you overstate.
suggestions.how: Pick people who will be honest. Listen without defending. Write down what you hear.
suggestions.check: You see your own pattern and adjust.

suggestions.title: Say 'I am not sure'
suggestions.do: Admit what you do not know without fear.
suggestions.how: Use it at least once per session where it is true.
suggestions.check: Others trust your confident statements more.

suggestions.title: Listen to the end
suggestions.do: Let others finish before you answer.
suggestions.how: Count to two after they stop. Repeat their key word.
suggestions.check: Others feel heard and you learn more.

suggestions.title: Compare your claims with your results
suggestions.do: Track claims you made and what happened.
suggestions.how: List five claims you made this month and the outcome. Note the gaps.
suggestions.check: Your claims match what you deliver.

suggestions.title: Decide first, ask after
suggestions.do: Make your own decision before you ask for views.
suggestions.how: Write your choice and a reason first, then ask. Compare.
suggestions.check: Your decisions are your own.

suggestions.title: Praise-free week
suggestions.do: Do a task and do not seek feedback on it.
suggestions.how: Finish it, judge it yourself against a standard, and leave it.
suggestions.check: Your satisfaction comes from the work.

suggestions.title: Set your own standards
suggestions.do: Write what good looks like for you in each task.
suggestions.how: Three criteria per task. Rate yourself against them.
suggestions.check: You judge yourself steadily.

suggestions.title: Hold an unpopular view politely
suggestions.do: State a view the group disagrees with, with a reason.
suggestions.how: Practise in safe groups. Stay calm and respectful.
suggestions.check: You can disagree and still feel fine.

suggestions.title: Add substance to style
suggestions.do: Prepare real content for each topic you speak on.
suggestions.how: Spend twice as long on content as on delivery. Keep facts and examples ready.
suggestions.check: Your content holds up when probed.

suggestions.title: Expect the follow-up question
suggestions.do: For every point, ask yourself 'and then?' and answer.
suggestions.how: Write the next two questions someone could ask and prepare answers.
suggestions.check: You are not caught out by follow-ups.

suggestions.title: Study a topic in depth
suggestions.do: Pick a topic and learn it deeply.
suggestions.how: Read three sources and explain it to a friend.
suggestions.check: You can speak confidently with detail.

suggestions.title: Tell the truth about your level
suggestions.do: Describe your abilities honestly in practice.
suggestions.how: Give an honest assessment and a plan to improve.
suggestions.check: Your confidence is based on facts.

suggestions.title: Face tougher rooms
suggestions.do: Practise with seniors or in a harder setting.
suggestions.how: Ask a mentor to challenge you in ONLINE mock rounds.
suggestions.check: Your confidence holds against seniors.

suggestions.title: Stay calm after a setback
suggestions.do: Rehearse a calm response to failure.
suggestions.how: Recover from a bad moment in practice within ten seconds.
suggestions.check: You bounce back quickly.

olq.name: Speed of Decision
olq.meaning: How quickly you reach a sound decision and commit to it, using the information at hand, without rushing or stalling.
olq.trainNote: SOD is trainable with timed practice. Advice differs by type: the slow decider needs speed drills, the hasty decider needs a checking habit.

tick.6: Adequate. You decide in reasonable time. The step up is deciding faster in unfamiliar or high-pressure situations.
tick.7: Restricted. You decide in simple situations and take time or help in complex ones.
tick.8: Limitation. Decisions are slow, hasty, avoided or changed repeatedly.
tick.9: Serious limitation. Decisions are rarely made on your own, so the basics of deciding need rebuilding.

olq.strength: Strength. You decide promptly and soundly. Keep testing it in unfamiliar, high-stakes situations.

patterns.label: Slow to decide, over-weighs options

seen.6: Decides well, a little slower than needed.
seen.7: Decides in simple matters and deliberates long in complex ones.
seen.8: Slow decisions. Weighs options for too long and the moment passes.
seen.9: Cannot decide without help.

patterns.root: Fear of the wrong choice. Wants complete information before committing.

patterns.label: Hasty, decides before thinking

seen.6: Decides quickly and mostly well, with an occasional rush.
seen.7: Decides fast and sometimes misses a key factor.
seen.8: Hasty and ill-considered decisions. Often has to reverse.
seen.9: Impulsive decisions that hurt the task.

patterns.root: Speed feels like strength. The check on the aim is skipped.

patterns.label: Avoids deciding, defers to others

seen.6: Decides, with a tendency to consult.
seen.7: Prefers to consult and follow the group's decision.
seen.8: Avoids decisions. Waits for others to decide and goes along.
seen.9: Never decides on own.

patterns.root: Dislikes owning the result. Safer to follow.

patterns.label: Changes decision repeatedly

seen.6: Decides and sticks, with an occasional second thought.
seen.7: Decides, then doubts and shifts under pushback.
seen.8: Unstable. Changes decisions with each new opinion.
seen.9: Cannot hold any decision.

patterns.root: Low confidence in the decision. Responds to the last voice heard.

patterns.label: Quick on routine, slow on the new

seen.6: Quick in familiar matters and takes a bit longer in new ones.
seen.7: Decides well in familiar territory and slowly in new.
seen.8: Freezes when the situation is unfamiliar.
seen.9: Cannot decide in any new situation.

patterns.root: Decisions rest on past patterns. Limited practice with unfamiliar choices.

patterns.label: Consolidate and stretch

seen.5: Strength. Keep testing it in unfamiliar, high-stakes situations.
seen.6: Decides in reasonable time. Gains come from speed under pressure and with less information.

patterns.root: Strong base. The gap to a stronger tick is pace under pressure.

suggestions.title: Decide in 30 seconds drill
suggestions.do: Practise picking an option within 30 seconds.
suggestions.how: Take ten daily mini choices, such as route, meal, order of tasks. Use a timer.
suggestions.check: Your decision time drops and you stop dwelling.

suggestions.title: Two options, one rule
suggestions.do: Narrow to two options and use one rule to choose.
suggestions.how: Pick the rule: fastest, safest, cheapest. Apply it and move.
suggestions.check: Choosing feels simple and quick.

suggestions.title: Accept 70 percent information
suggestions.do: Decide when you have about 70 percent of the facts.
suggestions.how: Ask 'What do I know now?'. If you can answer, decide.
suggestions.check: You stop waiting for perfect information.

suggestions.title: Timed GPE and CT rounds
suggestions.do: Practise tasks with short decision windows.
suggestions.how: Give yourself 90 seconds to decide in each practice task. Review the quality.
suggestions.check: Your quick decisions are sound.

suggestions.title: Ten second check
suggestions.do: Take ten seconds to check the aim before you decide.
suggestions.how: Ask 'Does this serve the aim and fit the time?'. If yes, go.
suggestions.check: Your quick decisions stop needing reversal.

suggestions.title: List what could go wrong
suggestions.do: Name the biggest risk before you commit.
suggestions.how: Spend 15 seconds on one risk and one fix.
suggestions.check: Fewer surprises after you decide.

suggestions.title: Review your last five decisions
suggestions.do: Record decisions and results and look for patterns.
suggestions.how: Three lines per decision. Note what you missed.
suggestions.check: You see what you tend to skip.

suggestions.title: Slow down only for big choices
suggestions.do: Keep speed for small choices and take care for large ones.
suggestions.how: Rate each choice small, medium or big. Give big ones a full minute.
suggestions.check: You match care to the stakes.

suggestions.title: Own one decision a day
suggestions.do: Make one decision alone and take the result.
suggestions.how: Pick a decision with real consequences, however small. Tell no one before.
suggestions.check: Owning a decision starts to feel normal.

suggestions.title: Speak first on a decision
suggestions.do: State your preferred decision before the group does.
suggestions.how: Say 'I would go with X because Y' first. Then listen.
suggestions.check: You lead the decision at least once per session.

suggestions.title: Low-stakes decisions for the group
suggestions.do: Take charge of small group decisions.
suggestions.how: Choose a meeting time, a place, a plan. Announce it and own it.
suggestions.check: Others look to you for decisions.

suggestions.title: Lead a short task
suggestions.do: Take the lead in a short task and make the calls.
suggestions.how: In practice rounds, be the leader and decide each step.
suggestions.check: You decide and carry the group.

suggestions.title: Write the decision and the reason
suggestions.do: Write your decision with its reason and keep it.
suggestions.how: Read the note before changing. Change only if the facts changed.
suggestions.check: You hold your decisions unless facts change.

suggestions.title: Change only for a new fact
suggestions.do: Revise a decision only when new facts arrive.
suggestions.how: Ask 'What is new?' before you change. Opinion alone does not count.
suggestions.check: You stop swaying with each voice.

suggestions.title: Present decisions with a reason
suggestions.do: Say your decision and reason in one sentence.
suggestions.how: Use 'We will do X because Y'. Hold it when asked.
suggestions.check: Others respect your decision and rarely push it aside.

suggestions.title: Defend a decision in a mock
suggestions.do: Defend your decision against a mentor's challenge.
suggestions.how: Make the case with reasons for five minutes.
suggestions.check: You hold a good decision under pressure.

suggestions.title: Practise unfamiliar scenarios
suggestions.do: Work through ten unfamiliar situations a week and decide quickly.
suggestions.how: Use what-if cards: fire, injury, delay, lost item. Decide in 30 seconds.
suggestions.check: New situations stop freezing you.

suggestions.title: Decide by principle
suggestions.do: Use two or three principles to decide in new situations.
suggestions.how: Examples: safety first, task first, then comfort. Apply and move.
suggestions.check: You decide fast even without precedent.

suggestions.title: Try new things weekly
suggestions.do: Do one new activity every week.
suggestions.how: A new route, a new sport, a new task. Notice how you decide.
suggestions.check: Unfamiliar situations feel manageable.

suggestions.title: Read case studies
suggestions.do: Read short decision cases and decide before reading the outcome.
suggestions.how: Take short real incidents and write your decision, then compare.
suggestions.check: Your decisions get closer to good outcomes.

suggestions.title: Decide with less information
suggestions.do: Practise deciding with limited facts.
suggestions.how: Give yourself half the usual information and decide in 30 seconds.
suggestions.check: Quality holds and speed rises.

suggestions.title: Decide under time pressure
suggestions.do: Make decisions with a short clock in group tasks.
suggestions.how: Set a timer in every GPE, review afterwards.
suggestions.check: Your quick decisions stay sound.

olq.name: Ability to Influence the Group
olq.meaning: How well others accept your lead, listen to your ideas, and move with you, without force and without being the loudest voice.
olq.trainNote: AIG is built through credibility, listening and clear proposals. Influence rises when SA, COOP and POE rise, and falls when the Aspirant pushes or hides.

tick.6: Adequate. The group listens and follows at times. The step up is steadier influence in tense or competitive moments.
tick.7: Restricted. You influence a few, or only when the group is comfortable.
tick.8: Limitation. The group does not follow, whether from silence, force, selfishness or weak ideas.
tick.9: Serious limitation. The group ignores or resists you, so the foundation of influence needs building.

olq.strength: Strength. The group listens and follows you. Keep earning it in competitive and tense moments.

patterns.label: Quiet, not heard

seen.6: Heard when they speak, and speaks less than the group needs.
seen.7: Ideas are sensible but spoken softly or late, so they miss the discussion.
seen.8: Silent or inaudible. The group does not register their contribution.
seen.9: No presence in the group.

patterns.root: Hesitation and low volume. Waits to be invited.

patterns.label: Pushes, loud, forces own view

seen.6: Influences well, with a slightly strong push.
seen.7: Influences by insistence more than by reason.
seen.8: Loud and forceful. Others comply or resist.
seen.9: Dominates and the group turns against them.

patterns.root: Mistakes pressure for influence. Does not check how others receive it.

patterns.label: Speaks, but ideas lack weight

seen.6: Heard, and ideas are sound but not distinctive.
seen.7: Speaks and ideas are ordinary, so others do not take them up.
seen.8: Ideas are weak or unworkable, so the group does not follow.
seen.9: Ideas are not taken seriously.

patterns.root: Quality of thought. Influence follows ideas the group can use.

patterns.label: Influences for own benefit

seen.6: Influences well, with some personal angle.
seen.7: Pushes plans that favour their own role.
seen.8: Self-serving. The group senses the agenda and pulls back.
seen.9: Manipulative. The group distrusts them.

patterns.root: Seeks credit. Trust is low because the group suspects the motive.

patterns.label: Starts strong, loses the group

seen.6: Strong start, with an occasional drift.
seen.7: Influences at the start and loses momentum.
seen.8: Cannot sustain the group's attention or commitment.
seen.9: Loses control quickly.

patterns.root: Energy at the start without follow-up or clear structure.

patterns.label: Consolidate and stretch

seen.5: Strength. Keep earning it in competitive and tense moments.
seen.6: The group listens and follows at times. Gains come from steadier influence in tension.

patterns.root: Strong base. The gap to a stronger tick is consistency in tense or competitive settings.

suggestions.title: Speak in the first two minutes
suggestions.do: Say something useful early in every discussion.
suggestions.how: Prepare an opening line. Speak early so you are part of the flow.
suggestions.check: You are part of the discussion from the start.

suggestions.title: Speak up so the back of the room hears
suggestions.do: Raise volume by about 20 percent and slow your pace.
suggestions.how: Practise recorded speech. Aim for clear, calm and audible.
suggestions.check: Others respond to your points.

suggestions.title: Link your point to someone else's
suggestions.do: Build on another person's idea to enter the discussion.
suggestions.how: Say 'Building on what Asha said...'. It is easier to be heard that way.
suggestions.check: Others respond and you are part of the flow.

suggestions.title: Run a small group
suggestions.do: Lead a small activity such as a study group.
suggestions.how: Plan it, run it, and give instructions to four or five people.
suggestions.check: People follow your instructions.

suggestions.title: Ask, do not tell
suggestions.do: Turn a command into a question.
suggestions.how: Say 'What if we...?' instead of 'We will...'. Wait for response.
suggestions.check: Others join willingly.

suggestions.title: Give reasons, not volume
suggestions.do: Back every point with a reason in a calm voice.
suggestions.how: Say 'Because...' and give one reason. Lower volume when you feel pushed.
suggestions.check: Others accept your points without pressure.

suggestions.title: Let someone else win a point
suggestions.do: Concede one point to others in each session.
suggestions.how: Say 'That is a good point, I agree'. Mean it.
suggestions.check: Others become more open to your views.

suggestions.title: Watch faces after you speak
suggestions.do: After each contribution, read how the group received it.
suggestions.how: Note nods, silence or frowns. Adjust the next point.
suggestions.check: You adjust your style to the group.

suggestions.title: Prepare two real ideas per topic
suggestions.do: Come with two workable ideas for each topic.
suggestions.how: Prepare ten common topics with an idea, a reason and an example.
suggestions.check: Others use your ideas.

suggestions.title: Make ideas usable
suggestions.do: Show how your idea works in three steps.
suggestions.how: Say 'This works by... first, second, third'.
suggestions.check: Others adopt your idea.

suggestions.title: Fix the idea, not the delivery
suggestions.do: Check that each idea is workable before speaking.
suggestions.how: Ask 'Will this work with these resources?' If not, drop it.
suggestions.check: Your ideas are accepted more often.

suggestions.title: Study how good ideas are built
suggestions.do: Watch group tasks done well and note how ideas were made.
suggestions.how: Review recorded tasks and mark good ideas and why they worked.
suggestions.check: You learn the type of ideas groups adopt.

suggestions.title: Offer an idea that costs you
suggestions.do: Suggest a plan where your role is smaller.
suggestions.how: Pick the best plan for the group even if your part is minor.
suggestions.check: The group trusts your motives.

suggestions.title: Say whose idea it is
suggestions.do: Credit others for the good ideas in the plan.
suggestions.how: Name the person and the idea every time.
suggestions.check: Others accept your lead because you are fair.

suggestions.title: Ask the quiet ones
suggestions.do: Draw out the quiet members before you decide.
suggestions.how: Ask each by name. Build the plan with them.
suggestions.check: The group follows you with willingness.

suggestions.title: Build trust through small acts
suggestions.do: Do small dependable acts for the group.
suggestions.how: Be on time, keep promises, share what you know.
suggestions.check: The group trusts you more.

suggestions.title: Plan the middle, not just the start
suggestions.do: Plan the middle and end of the task.
suggestions.how: Write one checkpoint at the halfway point and use it to re-energise the group.
suggestions.check: The group is still with you at the end.

suggestions.title: Check in with the group
suggestions.do: Ask the group how it is going halfway.
suggestions.how: Say 'Where are we? Any issues?'. Adjust the plan.
suggestions.check: You keep the group engaged.

suggestions.title: Keep a steady pace
suggestions.do: Maintain steady effort through the task.
suggestions.how: Do not burst early. Hold a pace that you can keep.
suggestions.check: Your effort holds to the end.

suggestions.title: Summarise progress aloud
suggestions.do: Summarise where the group is at intervals.
suggestions.how: Say 'We have done X, next is Y'. Keep it short.
suggestions.check: The group follows your lead through the task.

suggestions.title: Hold influence under tension
suggestions.do: Practise leading in tense or competitive groups.
suggestions.how: Join ONLINE rounds with strong personalities and keep calm.
suggestions.check: You keep influence when it gets tense.

suggestions.title: Win over a sceptic
suggestions.do: Persuade one sceptical group member with reasons.
suggestions.how: Listen first, find the concern, answer it.
suggestions.check: The sceptic moves with you.

olq.name: Liveliness
olq.meaning: How well you keep your spirits up and bring light and energy to a group, especially when conditions are dull or difficult.
olq.trainNote: LIV is a core quality. It is a habit of attitude that can be trained, and the advice depends on whether the Aspirant is serious, flat, forced or erratic.

tick.6: Adequate. You are cheerful and keep spirits up in most situations. The step up is lifting others in hard times.
tick.7: Restricted. You are cheerful in easy conditions, and spirits sag when it gets difficult or dull.
tick.8: Limitation. You are serious, flat, forced or moody, and the group feels the weight.
tick.9: Serious limitation. You rarely bring or hold spirits, so the basics of liveliness need building.

olq.strength: Strength. You keep spirits up and lift others. Keep carrying it into hard conditions.

patterns.label: Serious and stiff

seen.6: Cheerful, though somewhat serious.
seen.7: Serious by nature. Enters humour late and rarely.
seen.8: Too serious and stiff. Rarely smiles or lightens the mood.
seen.9: Grim and unsmiling throughout.

patterns.root: Takes the assessment too seriously. Equates seriousness with maturity.

patterns.label: Cheerful until it gets hard

seen.6: Cheerful, with a small dip under strain.
seen.7: Cheerful in comfort and low when conditions are hard.
seen.8: Spirits drop under strain. Looks tired and withdrawn.
seen.9: Collapses under difficulty.

patterns.root: Cheerfulness depends on comfort. Stamina is the real driver.

patterns.label: Forced cheerfulness

seen.6: Cheerful, with the odd forced note.
seen.7: Cheerful in a way that seems practised.
seen.8: Artificial humour or loud cheer that others read as insincere.
seen.9: Obviously acting. Others see through it.

patterns.root: Knows the OLQ is assessed and tries to display it.

patterns.label: Moody and erratic

seen.6: Mostly cheerful, with a minor mood swing.
seen.7: Cheerful when things go well and moody when they do not.
seen.8: Mood swings affect the group. Spirits are unpredictable.
seen.9: Sullen and affects the group's mood.

patterns.root: Mood tied to results or small irritations. Weak emotional regulation.

patterns.label: Quietly cheerful, not seen

seen.6: Cheerful, and low-key.
seen.7: Inwardly cheerful and does not show it.
seen.8: Reserved, so others read it as flat.
seen.9: Shows nothing, so the group assumes disinterest.

patterns.root: Shy about showing cheer. Fears that expression looks foolish.

patterns.label: Consolidate and stretch

seen.5: Strength. Keep carrying it into hard conditions.
seen.6: Cheerful and steady. Gains come from lifting others in hard conditions.

patterns.root: Strong base. The gap to a stronger tick is lifting the group when it is low.

suggestions.title: Smile at the start of every interaction
suggestions.do: Start each conversation with a real smile and a greeting.
suggestions.how: Practise with family and friends. Notice the response.
suggestions.check: Others warm up quickly and you look more approachable.

suggestions.title: Share light moments
suggestions.do: Share one light remark or story a day.
suggestions.how: A funny observation, a small story. Keep it gentle and not at anyone's expense.
suggestions.check: People enjoy your company.

suggestions.title: Play something for fun
suggestions.do: Join a game or sport for enjoyment, not for winning.
suggestions.how: Play twice a week with friends. Enjoy it out loud.
suggestions.check: You feel more relaxed and it shows.

suggestions.title: Seriousness for the task, lightness for the people
suggestions.do: Keep the task serious and your manner warm.
suggestions.how: Give the task full effort and still joke lightly with the group.
suggestions.check: People see both purpose and warmth.

suggestions.title: Physical stamina training
suggestions.do: Build fitness through regular training.
suggestions.how: Run, cycle or swim four times a week and increase intensity slowly.
suggestions.check: You stay cheerful in physically hard tasks.

suggestions.title: Practise cheer when tired
suggestions.do: In hard moments, deliberately lift your tone and posture.
suggestions.how: When tired, straighten up, breathe, say something encouraging. Do it in every practice session.
suggestions.check: Your spirits stay up when conditions are hard.

suggestions.title: Sleep and food basics
suggestions.do: Fix your sleep and meal routine.
suggestions.how: Sleep 7 to 8 hours, eat at set times, drink water. Track for four weeks.
suggestions.check: Your energy is steady through the day.

suggestions.title: Complete hard tasks, then celebrate
suggestions.do: Do something tough and mark the finish.
suggestions.how: A long run, a tough chore. Note how it felt when done.
suggestions.check: Difficulty stops draining your mood.

suggestions.title: Be yourself, lighter
suggestions.do: Use your natural humour and not borrowed jokes.
suggestions.how: Share what you actually find funny. Drop performances.
suggestions.check: Your cheer feels natural.

suggestions.title: Listen more, perform less
suggestions.do: Focus on others' cheer and respond to it.
suggestions.how: Laugh at what is funny. Do not try to be funny.
suggestions.check: Conversations feel relaxed.

suggestions.title: Be warm without showing off
suggestions.do: Pick small warm acts and not loud displays.
suggestions.how: Share food, ask after someone, offer to carry something.
suggestions.check: Others see warmth as natural.

suggestions.title: Spend time with people for no reason
suggestions.do: Hang out without an agenda.
suggestions.how: Spend time with a group of friends with no goal.
suggestions.check: You stop feeling the need to act cheerful.

suggestions.title: Name the mood, then choose
suggestions.do: Note when your mood shifts and decide how to act.
suggestions.how: Say to yourself 'I feel low. I will still...'. Choose the action.
suggestions.check: Mood changes no longer decide your behaviour.

suggestions.title: Keep a trigger list
suggestions.do: Write what triggers your mood drops.
suggestions.how: Note each drop and trigger for a month. Plan responses for the top two.
suggestions.check: You see triggers early and manage them.

suggestions.title: Reset routine
suggestions.do: Use a short reset when mood falls.
suggestions.how: Two minutes of breathing, water, a short walk. Return to the task.
suggestions.check: Mood recovers within minutes.

suggestions.title: Regular exercise for mood
suggestions.do: Exercise regularly to steady mood.
suggestions.how: 30 minutes, five days a week.
suggestions.check: Mood swings reduce.

suggestions.title: Show cheer visibly
suggestions.do: Let your face and voice show what you feel.
suggestions.how: Smile, nod, laugh out loud. Practise in front of a mirror.
suggestions.check: Others read you as cheerful.

suggestions.title: Add a light comment per session
suggestions.do: Say one light comment in every group session.
suggestions.how: A simple remark on the situation. Keep it short and kind.
suggestions.check: Others see your lighter side.

suggestions.title: Greet people by name
suggestions.do: Greet each person by name with warmth.
suggestions.how: Say 'Good morning, Neha!' with a smile. Do it for each person.
suggestions.check: You are seen as warm.

suggestions.title: Take part in group fun
suggestions.do: Join group activities, games and songs.
suggestions.how: Say yes to group fun. Take part fully.
suggestions.check: You are part of the group's lighter side.

suggestions.title: Lift the group when it is low
suggestions.do: When the group is down, do something to bring up spirits.
suggestions.how: A word of encouragement, a short rest, a light remark.
suggestions.check: The group's mood lifts because of you.

suggestions.title: Keep cheer through a long hard day
suggestions.do: Stay cheerful through physical and mental strain.
suggestions.how: Take on a long day such as a trek or event. Stay positive.
suggestions.check: You are cheerful at the end of a hard day.

olq.name: Determination
olq.meaning: How long and how steadily you keep going toward a goal when it gets hard, slow or unrewarding.
olq.trainNote: DET is trainable through repeated finishing of hard things. Advice differs by type: some Aspirants quit early, some persist in the wrong way, some are stubborn and not determined.

tick.6: Adequate. You persist through most difficulty. The step up is carrying on when results are slow or the setback is real.
tick.7: Restricted. You persist when progress is visible, and ease off when it is not.
tick.8: Limitation. You give up early, persist blindly, or hold on without adapting.
tick.9: Serious limitation. You drop goals at the first real difficulty, so the basics of persistence need building.

olq.strength: Strength. You keep going toward the goal under difficulty. Keep stretching with longer, harder goals.

patterns.label: Eases off or quits when it gets hard

seen.6: Persists well, with a slight slackening under strain.
seen.7: Works hard while it is going well and slackens when results slow.
seen.8: Gives up early. Drops goals under difficulty.
seen.9: Quits at the first real obstacle.

patterns.root: Motivation depends on quick results. Little experience of finishing hard things.

patterns.label: Stubborn, persists in a failing way

seen.6: Persistent, and a little slow to change method.
seen.7: Persists and is slow to change approach when it fails.
seen.8: Stubborn. Repeats the failing method and rejects advice.
seen.9: Rigid. Cannot let go of a failing plan.

patterns.root: Mistakes sticking to a method for determination. Pride or fear of admitting change.

patterns.label: Effort without clear aim

seen.6: Determined, with a goal that is sometimes loose.
seen.7: Works hard, but the aim is vague.
seen.8: Busy but aimless. Effort does not tie to an outcome.
seen.9: No aim and no persistence.

patterns.root: No written goal or milestones. Effort is spread across too many things.

patterns.label: Strong bursts, no steady pace

seen.6: Steady, with occasional uneven effort.
seen.7: Works in bursts and then rests.
seen.8: Intense effort that fades. Unsteady.
seen.9: Cannot keep effort going.

patterns.root: Enthusiasm outruns habit. Effort is not paced.

patterns.label: Needs a push or reward to continue

seen.6: Self-driven, with an occasional need for a push.
seen.7: Continues with encouragement or reward.
seen.8: Needs outside push to keep going.
seen.9: Stops without outside pressure.

patterns.root: The reason for the goal is borrowed from others and not owned.

patterns.label: Consolidate and stretch

seen.5: Strength. Keep stretching with longer, harder goals.
seen.6: Persistent and steady. Gains come from carrying on through slow results and real setbacks.

patterns.root: Strong base. The gap to a stronger tick is endurance of effort over a long period.

suggestions.title: Finish one hard thing a week
suggestions.do: Pick one difficult task a week and complete it.
suggestions.how: A long run, a tough chapter, a repair. Do not stop till done.
suggestions.check: Finishing hard things becomes normal.

suggestions.title: Just five more minutes
suggestions.do: When you want to stop, do five more minutes.
suggestions.how: Apply it to study, exercise, practice. Always do the extra five.
suggestions.check: Your quitting point moves later.

suggestions.title: Break the goal into small wins
suggestions.do: Split the goal into steps you can finish in a day.
suggestions.how: List daily targets and tick each one. Review on Sunday.
suggestions.check: Progress feels visible and you keep going.

suggestions.title: Long-term project with a deadline
suggestions.do: Commit to a project over several weeks.
suggestions.how: A fitness goal, a skill, a course. Set a date and report weekly to a mentor.
suggestions.check: You reach the date with the goal done.

suggestions.title: Review what is not working
suggestions.do: At fixed intervals, ask 'Is this method working?'.
suggestions.how: Review every 10 minutes in a task. If not, change the method and keep the aim.
suggestions.check: You hold the aim and change the method.

suggestions.title: Try an alternative on purpose
suggestions.do: In practice, switch methods after a failure.
suggestions.how: After a failed attempt, name two alternatives and pick one.
suggestions.check: You adapt without losing drive.

suggestions.title: Ask for advice and use one idea
suggestions.do: Ask a mentor or friend how they would try it.
suggestions.how: Take one idea from the advice and test it.
suggestions.check: You are open to advice without losing resolve.

suggestions.title: Separate pride from the goal
suggestions.do: Ask 'Am I doing this to win or to be right?'.
suggestions.how: Write the answer. If it is pride, switch.
suggestions.check: Your effort follows the goal.

suggestions.title: Write one clear goal
suggestions.do: Write one goal with a date and a measure.
suggestions.how: Example: 'Run 5 km in 28 minutes by 30 November'. Put it where you see it.
suggestions.check: Your effort ties to one clear outcome.

suggestions.title: Weekly milestones
suggestions.do: Set one measurable milestone per week.
suggestions.how: Review on Sunday and plan the next week.
suggestions.check: Progress is visible every week.

suggestions.title: Drop what does not matter
suggestions.do: Remove three activities that do not serve the goal.
suggestions.how: List current activities and cut those that do not add to the aim.
suggestions.check: Your energy goes to one goal.

suggestions.title: Explain your goal to someone
suggestions.do: Tell a mentor your goal and plan.
suggestions.how: Ask them to question it. Revise.
suggestions.check: You can state your goal and plan in two sentences.

suggestions.title: Daily minimum
suggestions.do: Set a daily minimum effort that you never skip.
suggestions.how: 20 minutes of study or exercise, every day. Never zero.
suggestions.check: A steady habit forms.

suggestions.title: Track streaks
suggestions.do: Track consecutive days of effort.
suggestions.how: Mark each day on a calendar. Do not break the chain.
suggestions.check: You hold a streak of 30 days.

suggestions.title: Pace your effort
suggestions.do: Spread effort evenly instead of bursts.
suggestions.how: Plan effort across the week. Rest by plan, not by collapse.
suggestions.check: Effort is steady across weeks.

suggestions.title: Endurance training
suggestions.do: Build endurance through regular physical training.
suggestions.how: Increase run time by 10 percent per week.
suggestions.check: Your effort lasts longer.

suggestions.title: Write your own reason
suggestions.do: Write why this goal matters to you personally.
suggestions.how: Three lines in your own words. Read it daily.
suggestions.check: Your drive comes from within.

suggestions.title: Set your own deadline and keep it
suggestions.do: Set deadlines without outside pressure.
suggestions.how: Pick a date and a penalty for yourself. Keep it.
suggestions.check: You finish without being pushed.

suggestions.title: Self reward after real effort
suggestions.do: Reward yourself for effort and not for results only.
suggestions.how: Pick a small reward after each milestone.
suggestions.check: You enjoy effort itself.

suggestions.title: Take on a goal nobody is checking
suggestions.do: Pursue a goal that no one will check.
suggestions.how: A skill or fitness target for yourself.
suggestions.check: You continue without watchers.

suggestions.title: Long, slow goals
suggestions.do: Take a goal that needs months.
suggestions.how: Set a monthly checkpoint and report to a mentor.
suggestions.check: You hold the goal over months.

suggestions.title: Recover after a real setback
suggestions.do: After a setback, set the next target within 24 hours.
suggestions.how: Write what you learned and the next step.
suggestions.check: You bounce back quickly.

olq.name: Courage
olq.meaning: How you act in the face of physical and moral risk: whether you take a reasonable risk, stand by your view and keep your head when it is uncomfortable.
olq.trainNote: COUR is a core quality and changes slowly. It needs graded exposure to real risk, both physical and moral, and the advice differs for fear, caution and recklessness.

tick.6: Adequate. You take reasonable risks and hold your view. The step up is steadiness when the risk is real.
tick.7: Restricted. You act in safe situations and hold back when the risk is real.
tick.8: Limitation. You avoid risk, give way under pressure or act recklessly without judgement.
tick.9: Serious limitation. Risk, physical or moral, stops you, so the basics of facing it need building.

olq.strength: Strength. You take reasonable risks and stand firm. Keep stretching to harder challenges.

patterns.label: Physically cautious, avoids physical risk

seen.6: Takes physical challenges, with a little caution.
seen.7: Hesitates before physical risk, then does it.
seen.8: Avoids or hesitates at physical tasks involving height, water or danger.
seen.9: Refuses physical risk.

patterns.root: Low exposure to physical challenge. Fear has not been worked through.

patterns.label: Gives way in the face of opposition

seen.6: Holds views, with occasional giving way.
seen.7: Holds a view in comfortable settings and gives way when pressed.
seen.8: Gives way to pressure. Does not speak against the group or a senior.
seen.9: Never stands against anyone.

patterns.root: Fear of conflict or of being disliked.

patterns.label: Reckless, takes risk without judgement

seen.6: Takes risks, and sometimes with limited calculation.
seen.7: Bold, with calculation that is thin.
seen.8: Reckless. Takes risks that are not required or not thought through.
seen.9: Dangerous. Risk without regard to consequences.

patterns.root: Mistakes daring for courage. Does not weigh risk against the aim.

patterns.label: Freezes or panics under real risk

seen.6: Steady, with a pause under real risk.
seen.7: Acts in training and slows in real danger.
seen.8: Freezes or panics when the risk is real.
seen.9: Panics visibly.

patterns.root: Stress response has not been trained. Fear overrides planned actions.

patterns.label: Brave in front of others, cautious alone

seen.6: Brave, with a slight lean to audience.
seen.7: Bold when watched and cautious when alone.
seen.8: Courage depends on the audience.
seen.9: Acts bravely only for display.

patterns.root: Driven by approval rather than conviction.

patterns.label: Consolidate and stretch

seen.5: Strength. Keep stretching to harder challenges.
seen.6: Takes reasonable risks and holds views. Gains come from steadiness when the stakes are real.

patterns.root: Strong base. The gap to a stronger tick is composure under real stakes.

suggestions.title: Graded exposure to your fear
suggestions.do: List physical fears and take a small step on one each week.
suggestions.how: Example for height: stand on a low wall, then a balcony, then a climbing wall. Never force it, step by step.
suggestions.check: You complete a step that was hard before.

suggestions.title: Adventure activity under a trainer
suggestions.do: Take part in a supervised activity such as swimming, trekking, climbing or rope work.
suggestions.how: Join a qualified group and attend regularly.
suggestions.check: You enjoy physical challenge with control.

suggestions.title: Strength and agility basics
suggestions.do: Build the fitness that supports physical confidence.
suggestions.how: Strength, balance, running. Three sessions a week.
suggestions.check: You feel capable of the physical tasks.

suggestions.title: Breathe and move
suggestions.do: In physical tasks, slow your breath and move steadily.
suggestions.how: Breathe slowly and take one move at a time.
suggestions.check: You stay steady during the task.

suggestions.title: Say the unpopular thing, politely
suggestions.do: Voice a respectful disagreement once a day.
suggestions.how: Say 'I see it differently because...'. Start with low-stakes topics.
suggestions.check: You voice a view without anxiety.

suggestions.title: Hold your view for one round
suggestions.do: When pushed, keep your view for one more exchange before deciding.
suggestions.how: Restate the reason and ask 'Which fact changes it?'.
suggestions.check: You hold a good view under pressure.

suggestions.title: Disagree with a senior, respectfully
suggestions.do: Practise a respectful disagreement with a senior or mentor.
suggestions.how: Prepare your point and say it clearly in an ONLINE mock.
suggestions.check: You can disagree with respect and calm.

suggestions.title: Stand up for someone
suggestions.do: Back a person who is being treated unfairly.
suggestions.how: Pick a small, real situation. Speak calmly and clearly.
suggestions.check: You act on what you believe is right.

suggestions.title: Ask 'is this risk needed'
suggestions.do: Before taking a risk, ask whether the aim requires it.
suggestions.how: Write the aim, the risk and the safer alternative.
suggestions.check: Your risks serve the aim.

suggestions.title: Calculate before you leap
suggestions.do: Spend 20 seconds weighing gain and loss before a risk.
suggestions.how: Name the best case, worst case and how you would recover.
suggestions.check: Your risks are bold and calculated.

suggestions.title: Safety discipline
suggestions.do: Follow safety rules in every physical activity.
suggestions.how: Use the correct gear, check the area and follow instructions.
suggestions.check: You stay bold within safe limits.

suggestions.title: Learn from near misses
suggestions.do: Record your risky moments and what you would change.
suggestions.how: Three lines for each. Read weekly.
suggestions.check: Your risk judgement improves.

suggestions.title: Stress inoculation
suggestions.do: Rehearse stressful situations in controlled settings.
suggestions.how: Simulate a stressful task in practice. Use breathing and a plan.
suggestions.check: Your response stays steady.

suggestions.title: First action drill
suggestions.do: Have a first action ready for common emergencies.
suggestions.how: For fire, injury or fall, memorise the first two actions and rehearse them.
suggestions.check: You act on the first step without delay.

suggestions.title: Controlled breathing
suggestions.do: Use box breathing before and during stress.
suggestions.how: In four, hold four, out four, hold four. Use it at the first sign of panic.
suggestions.check: Your heart rate settles and you think clearly.

suggestions.title: First aid and emergency training
suggestions.do: Attend basic first aid or emergency training.
suggestions.how: Join a local course and practise.
suggestions.check: You feel prepared and stay steady.

suggestions.title: Do one brave act unseen
suggestions.do: Do something brave and tell no one.
suggestions.how: Speak up for someone, try a hard thing alone.
suggestions.check: Courage stops depending on audience.

suggestions.title: Act on conviction
suggestions.do: Take a stand on something you believe in.
suggestions.how: Choose a belief and write why. Act on it in a small way.
suggestions.check: Your actions follow your values.

suggestions.title: Say no without an audience
suggestions.do: Refuse something that is wrong, in private.
suggestions.how: Pick a real situation. Say no calmly.
suggestions.check: You hold firm in private.

suggestions.title: Reflect on motives
suggestions.do: Ask 'Would I do this if nobody saw it?'.
suggestions.how: Write the answer for each brave act.
suggestions.check: Your courage is genuine.

suggestions.title: Take on a real challenge
suggestions.do: Take a challenge with real stakes.
suggestions.how: A solo trek, a tough competition, a public speech.
suggestions.check: You stay steady under real stakes.

suggestions.title: Stay steady with a senior opposing
suggestions.do: Hold a position under challenge from a senior.
suggestions.how: Practise in ONLINE mock interviews.
suggestions.check: You are calm under senior pressure.

olq.name: Stamina
olq.meaning: How long you keep working at full effort, physically and mentally, without your performance dropping.
olq.trainNote: STA is physical and mental and both are trainable. The advice differs by type: low physical fitness, mental fatigue, uneven pacing, or poor recovery.

tick.6: Adequate. You keep going through demanding days. The step up is staying sharp late in a long day.
tick.7: Restricted. You keep going through most tasks and tire noticeably near the end.
tick.8: Limitation. You tire early, fade in thinking, or burn out through uneven effort.
tick.9: Serious limitation. You cannot keep effort up through a normal day, so the basics of endurance need building.

olq.strength: Strength. You keep up full effort through long days. Keep building endurance.

patterns.label: Physically tires early

seen.6: Fit, with a little tiredness late.
seen.7: Handles physical tasks and tires noticeably by the end.
seen.8: Low physical endurance. Slows or stops in physical tasks.
seen.9: Cannot sustain physical effort.

patterns.root: Low fitness base and inconsistent training.

patterns.label: Mind fades through a long day

seen.6: Sharp, with a small decline late in the day.
seen.7: Performs well early and thinking slows by the end.
seen.8: Mental fatigue. Quality of ideas and speech drops across the day.
seen.9: Mind shuts down under sustained effort.

patterns.root: Poor sleep, poor routine and little experience of long mental work.

patterns.label: Burns out through uneven effort

seen.6: Steady, with an occasional rush.
seen.7: Starts hard and fades.
seen.8: Overspends early and has nothing left for the end.
seen.9: Collapses halfway.

patterns.root: No pacing. Treats every moment as a sprint.

patterns.label: Slow to recover between efforts

seen.6: Recovers in reasonable time.
seen.7: Performs and then needs time to recover.
seen.8: Needs long rest after effort. Back-to-back tasks drop sharply.
seen.9: Unable to return to full effort after fatigue.

patterns.root: Poor sleep, nutrition or fitness base.

patterns.label: Stops when uncomfortable, not exhausted

seen.6: Pushes through most discomfort.
seen.7: Pushes through some discomfort and stops at the rest.
seen.8: Stops at discomfort long before real limits.
seen.9: Quits at first discomfort.

patterns.root: Low tolerance for discomfort, not low capacity.

patterns.label: Consolidate and stretch

seen.6: Strong endurance. Gains come from staying sharp late in a long day.

patterns.root: Strong base. The gap to a stronger tick is performance late in long days.

suggestions.title: Build a running base
suggestions.do: Run or walk briskly four times a week and add distance slowly.
suggestions.how: Start at 20 minutes, add 10 percent each week. Log time and distance.
suggestions.check: You cover longer distances without stopping.

suggestions.title: Strength and circuit training
suggestions.do: Add bodyweight circuits twice a week.
suggestions.how: Push-ups, squats, planks, lunges. Three rounds.
suggestions.check: You hold effort longer in physical tasks.

suggestions.title: Mix cardio types
suggestions.do: Include swimming, cycling or skipping.
suggestions.how: Use two other cardio sessions a week.
suggestions.check: Your overall endurance improves.

suggestions.title: Daily movement habit
suggestions.do: Move every day, even for 20 minutes.
suggestions.how: Walk, stretch, play. No zero days.
suggestions.check: Fitness becomes a daily habit.

suggestions.title: Fix sleep
suggestions.do: Sleep 7 to 8 hours at set times.
suggestions.how: Same bed time, no screens for 30 minutes before sleep.
suggestions.check: You wake rested and stay sharp.

suggestions.title: Long focus blocks
suggestions.do: Practise 90 minute blocks of focused work.
suggestions.how: Start at 45 minutes and add 15 each week. Take five minute breaks.
suggestions.check: Your focus holds across blocks.

suggestions.title: Mock full day practice
suggestions.do: Simulate a full SSB style day of tasks.
suggestions.how: Run a full ONLINE mock day with back-to-back tasks. Review your quality by the hour.
suggestions.check: Your late-day quality matches your early quality.

suggestions.title: Nutrition and hydration
suggestions.do: Eat regular balanced meals and drink water.
suggestions.how: Three meals, two snacks, 2 to 3 litres of water.
suggestions.check: Energy stays steady through the day.

suggestions.title: Pace for the whole day
suggestions.do: Plan effort across the day.
suggestions.how: Use 70 percent effort early and save 30 percent for later.
suggestions.check: You finish strong, not spent.

suggestions.title: Interval and steady training
suggestions.do: Alternate easy and hard efforts in training.
suggestions.how: Run 2 minutes hard, 2 minutes easy, repeat.
suggestions.check: You learn pacing in your body.

suggestions.title: Know your fade point
suggestions.do: Find out when your effort drops and extend it.
suggestions.how: Log effort every 15 minutes in long tasks. Plan a small break before the drop.
suggestions.check: Your fade point moves later.

suggestions.title: Long slow efforts
suggestions.do: Practise long slow efforts such as a long walk or trek.
suggestions.how: Add 15 minutes each week.
suggestions.check: You hold a steady pace for hours.

suggestions.title: Cool down and stretch
suggestions.do: Use cool-down and stretching after every session.
suggestions.how: Five minutes of walking and stretching.
suggestions.check: You recover faster between sessions.

suggestions.title: Sleep and meals after effort
suggestions.do: Eat and sleep well after hard days.
suggestions.how: A protein meal within an hour and early sleep.
suggestions.check: You recover overnight.

suggestions.title: Back-to-back sessions
suggestions.do: Do two sessions in a day with a short gap.
suggestions.how: Morning run and evening circuit once a week.
suggestions.check: The second session holds up.

suggestions.title: Rest days by plan
suggestions.do: Schedule rest days.
suggestions.how: One full rest day a week and easy days after hard ones.
suggestions.check: You recover without losing progress.

suggestions.title: Go one more minute
suggestions.do: In training, continue one more minute after wanting to stop.
suggestions.how: Push past the first urge. Note how you feel.
suggestions.check: You learn that the first urge is not the limit.

suggestions.title: Cold-start the session
suggestions.do: Start training immediately without delay.
suggestions.how: Do not think. Put on shoes and begin.
suggestions.check: You train even when you do not feel like it.

suggestions.title: Log comfort versus limit
suggestions.do: Rate each stop as 'discomfort' or 'real limit'.
suggestions.how: After each session, write the reason you stopped.
suggestions.check: You see most stops are discomfort.

suggestions.title: Train with a partner
suggestions.do: Train with someone who pushes you.
suggestions.how: Match a training partner and agree targets.
suggestions.check: You hold effort longer with support.

suggestions.title: Late-day sharpness
suggestions.do: Practise tasks late in the day.
suggestions.how: Schedule your hardest tasks in the afternoon.
suggestions.check: Your late-day work is as sharp.

suggestions.title: Endurance challenge
suggestions.do: Take on a long endurance event.
suggestions.how: A half marathon, a long trek, a cycling event.
suggestions.check: You complete it with a steady pace.
